title: Course Outline
summary: Stage 3 training covering Zura Spa identity, basic anatomy, physiology, and client psychology for deeper professional competence.

sections.title: About This Course
paragraphs: The Stage 3: Zura Wellness Professional Course deepens the therapist's understanding of Zura Spa identity, the body, how massage affects wellness, and the psychological side of client care.
Each module includes focused topics and a clear learning outcome so therapists know what they are expected to understand and demonstrate.

sections.title: Module 1: Introduction to Zura Spa and the Zura Wellness Professional
list: The vision and mission of Zura Spa.
Who is a Zura Wellness Professional?
Difference between a regular massage therapist and a Zura Wellness Professional.
The importance of passion, care, and professionalism.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: At the end of this module, the therapist should understand the identity, values, and service expectations of Zura Spa.

sections.title: Module 2: Basic Anatomy for Massage Therapists
list: Major body systems every therapist should understand.
The back, neck, shoulders, arms, legs, and feet.
Areas to avoid or handle carefully.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should understand the basic body structure and know how massage affects different parts of the body.

sections.title: Module 3: Basic Physiology for Massage Therapists
list: How the body responds to touch.
Stress and its effect on the body.
Why hydration after massage is important.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should understand how massage supports relaxation, circulation, muscle relief, and general wellness.

sections.title: Module 4: Client Psychology and Spa Psychotherapy Basics
list: Understanding why clients come to a spa.
Stress, anxiety, tiredness, and emotional pressure.
How to make clients feel safe and respected.
Managing shy, quiet, talkative, angry, or emotional clients.
How to listen without overstepping boundaries.
Knowing when to escalate client concerns.
sections.closing: Learning Outcome: The therapist should understand that clients are not only bringing their bodies for massage; they may also be bringing stress, tension, emotions, and expectations.
